ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure is a light-yellow shaded triangle, with a right-angle mark at the lower-left vertex; the hypotenuse-like side from the lower-left vertex to the right tip is labeled 12 cm; at the right tip, the angle between this 12 cm side and the upper side is labeled 18°. Reasoning: According to the diagram, treat it as a right triangle, where 12 cm is a leg adjacent to the 18° angle, and the other leg is the opposite side of that angle. From tan(18°)=opposite/adjacent, obtain opposite = 12·tan(18°). The area A = 1/2·12·(12·tan(18°)) = 72·tan(18°) ≈ 72·0.324919696 = 23.3942, rounded to the hundredth is 23.39.

raw_record.question_text: Find the area of the triangle. Round to the nearest hundredth.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a right triangle: the bottom-left vertex has a right-angle marker, the side from that vertex to the right apex is labeled 12 cm, and the angle at the right apex between this 12 cm side and the top side is 18°. Treat the 12 cm side as one leg adjacent to the 18° angle. Use tangent to find the other perpendicular leg: opposite leg = 12·tan(18°). Then compute the area using the right-triangle formula A = (1/2)(leg)(leg) = (1/2)(12)(12·tan 18°), and round the resulting value to the nearest hundredth.
